lines.japanese: 「うわ、すげえひと……」
lines.english: “Whoa. What a crowd...”

lines.japanese: イベント会場は予想を上回る混雑ぶりだった。
lines.english: The event was far more crowded than I'd expected.

lines.japanese: 催事場のあるフロアから、二つ三つ下の階まで列が続いている。
lines.english: The line stretched from the event floor down another two or three stories.

lines.japanese: なんだ、フリファなんてもう終わってるのかと思ったら、まだまだ人気あるんじゃないか。この光景を米田優や望月紀奈子にも見せてやりたい。
lines.english: Here I'd thought the Frickies were washed up, but they were still plenty popular. I wished Yuu Yoneda and Kinako Mochizuki could see this.

lines.japanese: 「こりゃ当日券は無理かなあ」
lines.english: “Same-day tickets may be hopeless.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか、ざんねんだったね……」
lines.english: “Oh. That's too bad...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それならいっしょに買い物する？　今日の夕ごはん、お兄ちゃんえらんでいいよ」
lines.english: “Then do you want to go shopping with me? You can pick what we have for dinner tonight.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、でもダメモトで並んでみたいかなあ。こんだけの列に並ばせるわけにはいかないし、小鳩は買いもの行ってていいよ」
lines.english: “Hmm. I still want to try lining up, even if it's hopeless. I can't make you stand in a line this long, so you can go shopping, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、お兄ちゃんひとりで待つの、たいくつでしょ？　いっしょにいる」
lines.english: “No. You'll get bored waiting alone. I'll stay with you.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ……で、でも、買いものに行くのもやぶさかじゃないよ」
lines.english: “Oh... B-but I wouldn't mind going shopping either.”

lines.japanese: イベントには行ってほしくないものの、それを直接言いだすことは出来ない。ああ、うちの妹は、悪役に徹しきれないベビーフェイスだなあ。
lines.english: She did not want me to attend the event, yet she could not bring herself to say so. My little sister was too much of a babyface to commit to the villain role.

lines.japanese: 「もういいよ小鳩、一緒にアレキサンダーでも行って、昼ごはん食べようか」
lines.english: “It's all right, Kobato. Why don't we go to Alexander and have lunch together?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 俺は群衆のひしめき合う階段から、窓の外の街並へと目を移した。
lines.english: I took my eyes from the staircase packed with people and looked out the window at the city.

lines.japanese: 「ああでも、最近アレキサンダーも使いすぎてたから、変化ないかなあ。そだ、たまにはイタめしなんかどうだい？　森里君に教えてもらった、いい店があるんだ」
lines.english: “Actually, we’ve been eating at Alexander a lot lately. We could use a change. How about Italian for once? Morisato told me about a good place.”

lines.japanese: 「え、えっ？　だってお兄ちゃん、イベントは……？」
lines.english: “Wh-what? But what about your event?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、こんなに混んでるんじゃ仕方ないよ。きっとテレビで放送もするだろう。それでいいや」
lines.english: “With a crowd like this, it can't be helped. They'll probably show it on television. That's good enough for me.”

lines.japanese: 「で、でも、あんな楽しみにしてたのに……」
lines.english: “B-but you were looking forward to it so much...”

lines.japanese: 「っていうか本当は、昨日の夜そう決めてたんだ。小鳩、本当は俺に行ってほしくないんだろ？」
lines.english: “Honestly, I decided this last night. You don't actually want me to go, do you, Kobato?”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ分かるよ。普段どんだけお兄ちゃんが小鳩のこと見てると思ってるんだ。あ、でも俺、覗きとかストーキングとか全然ないけどね」
lines.english: “Of course I can tell. How closely do you think Big Brother watches you every day? Oh, but I've never peeped or stalked anyone in my life.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は俺への配慮から、俺がヨッくん──足利氏に逢うことを止めなかった。
lines.english: Out of concern for me, Kobato had not tried to stop me from seeing Yoshi—Mr. Ashikaga.

lines.japanese: だから俺も小鳩に配慮して、やっぱり彼に逢うことはやめよう。
lines.english: So out of concern for Kobato, I would choose not to see him after all.

lines.japanese: 彼に逢えば……彼の姿をこの眼で見れば、自分の中で何かがすっきりするという確信めいた予感はあった。
lines.english: I had something close to certainty that meeting him—seeing him with my own eyes—would clear something up inside me.

lines.japanese: だけど、いいんだ。俺は自分より小鳩を優先させたい。
lines.english: But that was all right. I wanted to put Kobato before myself.

lines.japanese: いままで彼女がずっと、自分より兄を優先してくれたように。
lines.english: Just as she had always put her brother before herself.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん……」
lines.english: “Big Brother...”

lines.japanese: 「な？　だから今日はいいよ。二人でデ……じゃない、お買い物しよう」
lines.english: “Okay? So forget it for today. The two of us can go on a da—shopping trip.”

lines.japanese: しかし小鳩は動かなかった。俺が腕を取って引こうとしても、歩きだす気配がない。
lines.english: But Kobato did not move. Even when I took her arm and tried to pull her along, she showed no sign of walking.

lines.japanese: 「えっと……」
「おに、お兄ちゃんちょっといい？」
lines.english: “B-Big Brother, can we talk?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、どした？　結婚かい？」
lines.english: “Sure. What is it? Marriage?”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そゆのじゃなくて。ちょっとこっち」
lines.english: “N-not that. Come over here.”

lines.japanese: 冗談に乗る素振りも見せず、俺を柱のそばへ引っぱった。
lines.english: She did not even pretend to play along with the joke. She pulled me over beside a pillar.

lines.japanese: 「どしたんだ小鳩。なんなら場所変えるか？」
lines.english: “What's wrong, Kobato? We can go somewhere else if you want.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、ここでいい。外でたら、列がすすんじゃうかもしれないし」
lines.english: “No, here is fine. If we go outside, the line might move.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、お兄ちゃんはその……フリッキー５、好きだよね」
lines.english: “Um, Big Brother... You like Fricky Five, right?”
“Like them...?”

lines.japanese: 唐突だった。フリファを好きかどうか。ふむ、いざ好きかどうかなんて問われると──
lines.english: The question came out of nowhere. Did I like the Frickies? Hmm. Asked directly whether I liked them—

lines.japanese: 「うーん、好きっていうか、憧れに近いのかもな。昔から見てたし」
lines.english: “I don't know if ‘like’ is the word. Maybe it's closer to admiration. I've watched them since I was little.”

lines.japanese: 正直なところ、自分でも理由はよく分からない。気付いたら肉料理が好物だったようなものだ。
lines.english: Honestly, I did not understand the reason myself. It was like realizing one day that meat had always been my favorite food.

lines.japanese: あえて言うなら──言うまでもないことだが──間違いなく母の影響だろう。洗脳と言ってもいいかもしれない。
lines.english: If forced to name a reason—and this hardly needed saying—it was undoubtedly my mother's influence. One might even call it brainwashing.

lines.japanese: 幼少時代の俺は、来る日も来る日も、テレビ越しの彼らのパフォーマンスを見せられていたのだから。
lines.english: Day after day throughout my childhood, she had made me watch their performances on television.

lines.japanese: そして。
lines.english: And...

lines.japanese: 俺も小鳩も叔父さんたちも、誰ひとり口にこそしないけれど──
lines.english: Neither Kobato, my aunt and uncle, nor I ever said it aloud—

lines.japanese: ──いや、あまりに不自然なほど口をつぐんでいるからこそ、かえって明確な事実。
lines.english: —and precisely because our silence was so unnatural, the fact became all the clearer.

lines.japanese: 彼は、足利美樹は、俺の父親なのだろう。
lines.english: He—Yoshiki Ashikaga—was probably my father.

lines.japanese: 少なくとも俺は、母が愛した男性を他に知らない。
lines.english: At the very least, I knew of no other man my mother had loved.

lines.japanese: 「で、でもあのリーダーのひとって、お兄ちゃんのお母さんを泣かせたひとだよ」
lines.english: “B-but their leader made your mother cry.”

lines.japanese: 違いない。経緯や世の風聞がどうあれ、結果として、俺の母が彼を想って絶えず悲嘆に暮れる年月を送っていたのは事実だ。
lines.english: That was true. Whatever the circumstances or public gossip, my mother had spent years grieving ceaselessly for him.

lines.japanese: そのことで小鳩は、彼をよく思えないのだろう。
lines.english: That was why Kobato could not think well of him.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんは会っても平気なの？」
lines.english: “Will you be okay if you meet him?”
“What, me?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩が、ではなく……？
lines.english: She meant me, not herself...?

lines.japanese: 「うん。お兄ちゃんがあのひとに会ったりしたら、昔のことを思いだしちゃったりするかもしれないし……」
lines.english: “Yes. If you meet that man, you might remember things from the past...”

lines.japanese: 「それでお兄ちゃんが、またつらい思いしたりするのは嫌だよ」
lines.english: “I don't want you to suffer again.”

lines.japanese: ああ。
lines.english: Oh.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうだったのか……。
lines.english: Oh. So that was it...

lines.japanese: 小鳩が俺と彼を近付けたがらなかったのは、感情的な我が儘からではなく、俺の病状を心配してのことだったのか。
lines.english: So Kobato hadn’t been trying to keep us apart out of selfishness. She’d been worried about my condition.

lines.japanese: そんな気配りにも気付かないで、俺はひとりで馬鹿みたいに浮かれて、あまつさえ最初は小鳩を誘ったりして……まったく、情けないやら恥ずかしいやらだ。
lines.english: I had failed to notice even that. I'd gotten excited like an idiot, even invited Kobato at first... I felt pathetic and ashamed.

lines.japanese: 「俺、あのひとに逢って確かめたいことがあるんだ」
lines.english: “There's something I want to find out by meeting him.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩に対する後ろめたさか、自然と口が開いていた。
lines.english: Perhaps guilt toward Kobato opened my mouth.

lines.japanese: 「それはなんていうか、やっぱり俺の昔のことで……自分の中でも、どこか曖昧にしてたことなんだけど……」
lines.english: “It's about my past, or... something I've kept vague even in my own mind...”

lines.japanese: それはタカシだった俺が、意図もせずウェブ上で偶然拾った与太話。
lines.english: A wild story Takashi had stumbled across online by accident.

lines.japanese: あるいは鷲介が読んだ、ＤＩＤの青年を描く海の向こうの物語。
lines.english: Or an overseas story Shuusuke had read about a young man with DID.

lines.japanese: あるいは隼人が小耳に挟んだ、業界に伝わるテレビの裏の古い話。
lines.english: Or an old backstage television story Hayato had overheard within the industry.

lines.japanese: あるいは叔父夫妻がふすまの向こうで囁いていた、子供には聞かせたくない深刻な事情。
lines.english: Or a grave matter my aunt and uncle had whispered about beyond the sliding door, never intending a child to hear.

lines.japanese: 幾つかの形で、記憶の隅に引っかかっていた情報の断片。
lines.english: Fragments of information that had caught in the corners of my memory in several different forms.

lines.japanese: いわく、解離性同一性障害は、親から子へ遺伝するケースも無くはないという。
lines.english: One claimed that dissociative identity disorder could, in some cases, pass from parent to child.

lines.japanese: いわく、かつて隆盛を誇ったある男性グループの解散した要因は、リーダーを務める青年の精神的な破綻だったという。
lines.english: Another claimed that a once-dominant male group's breakup had been caused by the young leader's psychological collapse.

lines.japanese: それら眉唾ものの話にいかほどの信憑性があるのか、そんなことは知らない。調べる気もない。
lines.english: I did not know how much truth those dubious stories held. I had no intention of investigating.

lines.japanese: ただ、それがもとで、俺の中にひとつの仮説が浮かんだ。
lines.english: But they had planted one hypothesis in my mind.

lines.japanese: もしも俺の親が、俺と同じような障害を抱えていたとしたら──
lines.english: What if one of my parents had suffered from the same disorder as me?

lines.japanese: たとえば──
lines.english: For example—

lines.japanese: 羽田つぐみが出逢い、愛しあったのが、足利美樹ではない足利美樹だったとしたら──
lines.english: What if the Yoshiki Ashikaga whom Tsugumi Haneda had met and loved was a different Yoshiki Ashikaga—

lines.japanese: ──しかし、仮定がそこまで及んだとき、俺は恐怖にも似た躊躇を覚えて思考を止めた。
lines.english: But when my supposition reached that point, I felt a hesitation bordering on fear and stopped thinking.

lines.japanese: 考えたところで確証の得られないことだと、闇から背を向けるように自己完結させた。
lines.english: I told myself there was no way to prove it by thought alone and turned my back on the darkness.

lines.japanese: ところが、思いがけぬこの機会が訪れた。
lines.english: Then this unexpected opportunity arose.

lines.japanese: 「もう逃げないって小鳩と約束したからさ。曖昧にしておくのはやっぱり、その……良くないかなって」
lines.english: “I promised you I wouldn't run away anymore. So leaving it vague still feels... wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「それは、直接逢っても答えが出ないことかもしれないけど、なにか感じられる部分はあると思うんだ」
lines.english: “Meeting him in person may not give me an answer, but I think I'll sense something.”

lines.japanese: 具体的な仮説こそ挙げなかったが、俺にそれなりの意図があってこの場へ赴いたことまでは伝えた。
lines.english: I did not spell out my hypothesis, but I told her enough to convey that I had come here for a reason.

lines.japanese: 「それで今日、少しでも話せたらと思ったんだけど」
lines.english: “So I hoped I might at least speak with him today.”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん……」
lines.english: “Big Brother...”

lines.japanese: 「そうだったんだ……私、なにも知らないのに、よやくのジャマまでしちゃってごめん……」
lines.english: “I didn't know... I'm sorry I even got in the way of your reservation...”

lines.japanese: 「いや、小鳩が謝ることじゃないよ」
lines.english: “You have nothing to apologize for, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 言わなかった俺が悪いんだ。
lines.english: I was at fault for not telling her.

lines.japanese: いや、言うも何も、俺自身でさえ漠然と“逢ってみたかった”だけで、最初からこんな自分探しみたいな深いことを意識していたわけじゃない。
lines.english: Then again, there had been nothing definite to tell. Even I had only vaguely wanted to meet him. I had not consciously set out on some profound search for myself.

lines.japanese: 「だから今日はやめて、次の機会に…………あれ？」
lines.english: “So let's forget it today and wait for another chance... Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺のまとめを最後まで聞かずに、小鳩は走りだしていた。
lines.english: Before I could finish, Kobato ran off.

lines.japanese: 向かった先は、ひとが列なす狭い階段。入場待機列の最後尾だ。
lines.english: She headed toward the narrow staircase packed with people: the end of the admission line.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、すみません、チケットはあと何まい残ってますかっ」
lines.english: “E-excuse me! How many tickets are left?”

lines.japanese: テンパった小鳩は、係員でもない一般客のおばさんに食いついて、相手をビビらせていた。
lines.english: In her panic, Kobato pounced on an ordinary middle-aged customer rather than an employee and frightened the woman.

lines.japanese: 「い、いいよ小鳩、今日はもう本当に」
lines.english: “It's all right, Kobato. Really. Let's forget it today.”

lines.japanese: 「だ、だって私、お兄ちゃんのジャマしちゃって……」
lines.english: “B-but I got in your way...”

lines.japanese: それは俺の為を想ってしたことなんだろう？　だったら、俺の方こそ、おまえの気も知らずにはしゃいじゃってごめんな。
lines.english: You had done it because you cared about me. I was the one who should apologize for getting carried away without understanding how you felt.

lines.japanese: 俺は小鳩の手を引いて、帰ろうと促した。
lines.english: I took Kobato's hand and urged her to leave.

lines.japanese: しかし彼女は頑固に首を振った。
lines.english: But she stubbornly shook her head.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんが逃げないって決めたことなら、わた、私もきょうりょくしたい」
lines.english: “If you've decided not to run away, th-then I want to help too.”

lines.japanese: 俺の手を振りほどき、今度は別の客にチケットの入手方法を尋ねだした。
lines.english: She pulled free of my hand and asked another customer how she might get a ticket.
“Kobato...”

lines.japanese: おそらくもうイベントに参加は出来ないだろう。当日券があるかも分からないし、あったとしてもこの人気では無理だ。
lines.english: We probably could no longer attend the event. We did not even know whether same-day tickets existed, and with this crowd, any supply would be hopeless.

lines.japanese: しかし、人見知りの小鳩がそこまでしてくれる、その気持ちが有難かった。
lines.english: But I was grateful that shy little Kobato would go so far for me.

lines.japanese: 「よし、それならお兄ちゃんも頑張るぞ！　今からでも並ぼう。もしかしたらキャンセル百人出るかもしれないしな！」
lines.english: “All right! Then Big Brother will work hard too! Let's get in line even now. Maybe a hundred people will cancel!”

lines.japanese: 「う、うんっ。私も付きあう」
lines.english: “O-okay! I'll wait with you.”

lines.japanese: ありがとう……ありがとう小鳩……！
lines.english: Thank you... Thank you, Kobato...!

lines.japanese: 「小鳩ォー！」
lines.english: “Kobatooo!”

lines.japanese: 俺は照れ臭さもあって、いつものように、抱きつかんばかりの感激アピールでおどけてしまった。
lines.english: Partly to hide my embarrassment, I fell into my usual clowning, making a grand show of emotion as if about to throw my arms around her.

lines.japanese: そうしたら、ちょうど上の階から下りてきた、通りすがりの正義漢に怒られた。
lines.english: A righteous fellow happened to be coming down from the floor above and scolded me.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん。並んでる他のお客さんに迷惑ですから、階段で騒がないでください」
lines.english: “Chitose, don't make a scene on the stairs. You're bothering everyone in line.”

lines.japanese: 正義漢というか正義女子だった。
lines.english: A righteous young lady, rather.

lines.japanese: というか、なんと、ずっと探していた相手だった。
lines.english: And, in fact, the very person I had been searching for all along.

lines.japanese: 「玉泉ぃーっ！」
lines.english: “Tamaizumiii!”

lines.japanese: 「ほ、ほそ川せんせーは、どうしてここに？」
lines.english: “M-Ms. Hosokawa, what are you doing here?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええ、私もこれから、母が勝手にイベントのチケットを取ってしまったので、それを消化しに……」
lines.english: “Y-yes, well, my mother bought event tickets without asking me, so I came to use them...”

lines.japanese: ん？　なんか玉泉日和子、顔赤くないか？　なんか隠してるのか？
lines.english: Hm? Was Hiyoko Tamaizumi blushing? Was she hiding something?

lines.japanese: ひょっとして本当は、こいつもフリファが好きなんじゃ……はは、なーんて、そんなことあるわけ──
lines.english: Could she secretly like the Frickies too...? Hahaha. No, that was imposs—

lines.japanese: 「そういう千歳さんこそ、どうしてこの列に並んでるんですか？　あ、もしかして、フリファのイベントの列に並ぶくらい好きとか。はは、なーんて、そんなことあるわけ――」
lines.english: “Why are *you* in this line, Chitose? Don't tell me you like the Frickies enough to line up for their event. Hahaha. No, that would be imposs—”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうなんだ！　こう見えてフリッキー５に関しては誰にも負けない情熱を持っているぞ！」
lines.english: “That's exactly right! I may not look it, but no one can match my passion for Fricky Five!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 玉泉日和子は目を丸くした。こんな大昔のアイドルなんて、と引かれたのだろうか。
lines.english: Hiyoko Tamaizumi's eyes widened. Perhaps she was appalled that I cared about some ancient idol group.

lines.japanese: ああ、いまは笑ってくれて結構。
lines.english: Go ahead and laugh for now.

lines.japanese: その代わりフリファ大好きな俺から、大して好きでもないのにこの場にいるおまえへ、一生の頼みがある。俺は白々しく切りだした。
lines.english: In exchange, this devoted Frickies fan had a once-in-a-lifetime favor to ask of someone who barely cared about them. I broached it with studied innocence.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ。玉泉のひと、チケット一枚余ってるんだよな」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Tamaizumi, you have one extra ticket, don’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　ええ、そうですね余ってますが、どうしてそれを？」
lines.english: “What? Yes, I do, but how did you know?”

lines.japanese: いや、実は渡来明日香から聞いて……と説明しようとした俺を、小鳩が押しのけて前へ踊りでた。
lines.english: I was about to explain that Asuka Watarai had told me when Kobato shoved past me and sprang forward.

lines.japanese: 「あのっ！」
lines.english: “Excuse me!”

lines.japanese: 「あの、その余ってるチケット、ゆずっていただけませんか」
lines.english: “Um, could you please let us have your extra ticket?”

lines.japanese: 「え、チケットですか……？」
lines.english: “My ticket...?”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい。私はいいので、一枚だけでも！」
lines.english: “Y-yes. I don't need one. Just one, please!”

lines.japanese: 唖然とする玉泉日和子の前で、小鳩は深々と頭を下げた。
lines.english: Kobato bowed deeply before the stunned Hiyoko Tamaizumi.

lines.japanese: 「どうしても必要なんです。おねがいしますっ！」
lines.english: “We really need it. Please!”

lines.japanese: 必死なその姿に、俺も釣りこまれて頭を下げた。
lines.english: Her desperate posture pulled me into a bow as well.

lines.japanese: 「お、俺からも頼むっ！　定価の倍……いや、それに加えて、今後アレキサンダーでは真面目に働くから、売ってくれないか！」
lines.english: “I-I'm begging you too! I'll pay twice the price—no, I'll work seriously at Alexander from now on too! Would you sell it to me?”

lines.japanese: 突然わけの分からぬ要求を突きつけてきた兄妹は、玉泉日和子からすればさぞかし迷惑な存在だっただろう。
lines.english: From Hiyoko Tamaizumi's perspective, the siblings who had suddenly assaulted her with this incomprehensible demand must have been a tremendous nuisance.

lines.japanese: 彼女はしばらく無言で固まっていた。
lines.english: She stood frozen in silence for a while.

lines.japanese: 他にすべのない俺と小鳩は、彼女の善意にすがりついて、ただひただすら祈ることしか出来なかった。
lines.english: With no other recourse, Kobato and I could only cling to her goodwill and pray with all our might.

lines.japanese: やがて玉泉日和子が「そこまでおっしゃるなら……」などと言いながら鞄を探りだした。
lines.english: At last, muttering something like “If it means that much to you...” Hiyoko Tamaizumi began rummaging through her bag.

lines.japanese: 「……あの、これ」
lines.english: “...Here.”

lines.japanese: すっ、と俺たちの前に、紙製のチケットホルダーが差しだされる。
lines.english: She smoothly held out a paper ticket holder.

lines.japanese: 俺と小鳩は目を輝かせた。
lines.english: Kobato's eyes and mine lit up.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ありがとうございますっ！」
lines.english: “Th-thank you so much!”

lines.japanese: 「すまない、恩に着る！　この借りは必ず返すぞ、玉泉……ってあれ？　これ、二枚あるぞ？」
lines.english: “Thank you! I owe you one, Tamaizumi... Wait. There are two tickets in here.”

lines.japanese: 中を確認すると、続き数字の指定席券がふたり分。一枚でいいって言ったのに、それじゃ彼女自身はどうするつもりなんだろう。
lines.english: Inside were two consecutively numbered reserved-seat tickets. We'd asked for one. What did she intend to do herself?
“Sigh...”

lines.japanese: なぜか玉泉日和子は目を逸らしていた。
lines.english: For some reason, Hiyoko Tamaizumi looked away.

lines.japanese: 「どうしても必要なんですよね。それなら、お二人で一緒に観にいった方がいいんじゃないですか」
lines.english: “You truly need them, don't you? Then shouldn't the two of you watch together?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、だって自分の分は……」
lines.english: “What? But what about yours...?”

lines.japanese: 「必要なんですよね？」
lines.english: “You need them, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ」
lines.english: “Y-yes.”

lines.japanese: 「ならどうぞ。千歳さんのファンとしての心に打たれました。定価でお譲りします」
lines.english: “Then take them. Your devotion as a fan moved me, Chitose. I'll sell them to you at face value.”

lines.japanese: 「玉泉……お、おまえってやつは……」
lines.english: “Tamaizumi... Y-you...”

lines.japanese: そのとき俺の目には、慈悲をかけてくれた玉泉日和子がまるで女神のように見えた（つまり小鳩のように見えたってことだね）。気のせいだったけど。
lines.english: At that moment, the merciful Hiyoko Tamaizumi looked like a goddess to me—which is to say, she looked like Kobato. It was only my imagination.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんが真面目に働いてくれるというのも魅力的な提案ですし。これからはきちんとお願いしますね」
lines.english: “Your offer to work seriously is attractive as well. I expect you to do your job properly from now on.”

lines.japanese: くっ、玉泉のひとよ、なんていいやつなんだ。俺はおまえのような友を持って嬉しいぞ。部屋に貼ってある『生理休暇でつかまえて』の限定ポスターを差しあげたいくらいだ。
lines.english: Damn, Tamaizumi. What a wonderful friend. I was so glad to know you, I could almost give you the limited-edition *Catch Me on Menstrual Leave* poster hanging in my room.

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ほんと！？」
lines.english: “What? Really?!”

lines.japanese: うっかり漏れていた独り言に、がっつり喰いつかれた。
lines.english: She pounced on the thought I'd accidentally spoken aloud.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ゴメ。やっぱそれは無理。っていうか、やっぱフリファ好きなんじゃん」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. I can't give that up after all. And you *do* like the Frickies!”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ、母に喜んでもらえると思っただけです……それでは私はこれで」
lines.english: “N-no. I merely thought my mother would appreciate it... Now, if you'll excuse me.”

lines.japanese: 難しい顔をして、逃げるように玉泉日和子は去っていった。
lines.english: Hiyoko Tamaizumi fled with a troubled expression.

lines.japanese: あいつ……怪しいな……今度カラオケに行ったら『微笑みジェノサイド』の合いの手パートで、咄嗟にマイクを向けてみるか。
lines.english: Suspicious... Next time we went to karaoke, I would thrust the microphone at her during the audience-response part of *Smiling Genocide* and see how she reacted.

lines.japanese: 「お、お兄ちゃん、よかったね！」
lines.english: “B-Big Brother, that's great!”

lines.japanese: おっとと。そうだ、小鳩にもちゃんと礼を言わないとな。
lines.english: Oh, right. I needed to thank Kobato properly too.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ほんと良かった。小鳩のお陰だ」
lines.english: “Yes. This is wonderful. It's thanks to you, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、私、何もしてないよ。ほそ川せんせーがチケットゆずってくれたんだし」
lines.english: “No, I didn't do anything. Ms. Hosokawa gave us the tickets.”
“No—”

lines.japanese: 時代錯誤と笑われてきた俺には分かる。本当は玉泉日和子もきっと隠れフリファーなんだ。
lines.english: As someone mocked for being behind the times, I could tell. Hiyoko Tamaizumi was surely a closet Frickies fan.

lines.japanese: にも関わらずチケットを譲ってくれたのは、小鳩の真剣さが伝わったからに違いない。
lines.english: If she had surrendered her tickets despite that, it could only be because Kobato's earnestness had reached her.

lines.japanese: だから俺は、小鳩の頭を優しく撫でた。
lines.english: So I gently stroked Kobato's head.

lines.japanese: 「──ありがとう」
lines.english: “—thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「えへっ」
lines.english: “Heehee.”

lines.japanese: 「それにしても、すごい列だな。これに並んでたら、どれくらいかかったか……玉泉は定価でいいって言ってくれたけど、他にも何かしらお礼しないと……ん？」
lines.english: “Still, what a line. Who knows how long we'd have waited... Tamaizumi only asked face value, but we should thank her some other way too... Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　なんだろ、上の階からどんどんひとが下りてき――」
lines.english: “Huh? What's happening? People are pouring down from the floor ab—”

lines.japanese: 「フリッキー５のイベント『災い転じて服を剥ぐ』へお越しのお客様にご連絡いたします。本日行われるイベントにおいて、急遽、参加者の変更がございます」
lines.english: “Attention, guests attending the Fricky Five event *Every Cloud Has a Stripped Lining*. There has been a last-minute change to today's participants.”

lines.japanese: な、なに、参加者の変更だと！？　まさか足利ヨッくんが急遽欠席とか言うんじゃないだろうな！
lines.english: Wh-what? A change in participants?! They had better not say Yoshi Ashikaga was suddenly absent!

lines.japanese: 「個人的な事情により、細川隆一氏が不参加となりました。従って本日は細川氏を除いた四名でのイベントになります。繰りかえします、フリッキー５のイベント『災い転じて服を剥ぐ』へお越しの――」
lines.english: “Due to personal circumstances, Ryuuichi Hosokawa will not attend. Today's event will therefore feature the remaining four members without Mr. Hosokawa. To repeat: guests attending the Fricky Five event *Every Cloud Has a Stripped Lining*—”

lines.japanese: なるほど。ああ、なるほど。
lines.english: I see. Ah, I see.

lines.japanese: 今も昔もフリファのエース、いまだ芸能界の一線で活躍している、あの天下のホソリュー様が欠席ですかそうですか。
lines.english: Hosoryuu, the ace of the Frickies past and present, the great star still active at the front lines of show business, would be absent. I see.

lines.japanese: なるほど。ああ、なるほど。
lines.english: I see. Ah, I see.

lines.japanese: お客さんたちが突然ぞろぞろ帰りはじめたのは、そういうことですか。
lines.english: That was why customers had suddenly begun streaming home.

lines.japanese: 皆さん懐かしいフリファの歌を聴きにいらしたわけではなく、単に二枚目俳優・細川隆一を観に来ただけでしたか。
lines.english: None of you came to hear the nostalgic Frickies songs. You only wanted to see the handsome actor Ryuuichi Hosokawa.

lines.japanese: なるほど。ああ、なるほど。
lines.english: I see. Ah, I see.

lines.japanese: いま玉泉日和子が上から下りてきたのも、そしてやけにあっさりチケットを譲ってくれたのも……ああ、ああ、なるほど、そういうことでしたか。
lines.english: So that was why Hiyoko Tamaizumi had just come down from above, and why she had surrendered the tickets so easily... Ah. Ah, I see. Now it all made sense.

lines.japanese: あーははは。あまりにも混んでるからおかしいと思った。やっぱり現在のフリファはそんなもんですよねー。
lines.english: Ahahaha. I knew something was wrong when I saw that crowd. Of course this was all the modern-day Frickies could draw.

lines.japanese: くそう！
lines.english: Damn it!

lines.japanese: 「うわ、思ってたより空いてるな。ていうかまだ席が埋まってないし」
lines.english: “Whoa. It's emptier than I expected. The seats aren't even full.”

lines.japanese: 「はあー、ホソリューさん人気あるんだね」
lines.english: “Wow. Hosoryuu must be very popular.”

lines.japanese: 「さて、近い席だといいんだが……あっ！」
lines.english: “Now, I hope our seats are close... Ah!”

lines.japanese: 「ふわっ！？　え、ど、どうしたの」
lines.english: “Eep! Wh-what is it?”

lines.japanese: 「よよよヨッくんがステージ脇にいる！」
lines.english: “Y-Y-Yoshi is standing beside the stage!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 見れば簡易ステージは、関係者以外が立ち入りできぬよう、テープと数人のセキュリティによって防護されている。
lines.english: The makeshift stage was protected by tape and several security guards to keep unauthorized people away.

lines.japanese: 派手な衣装をまとった足利氏がその向こう、バックステージ前に立っていた。
lines.english: Beyond them, in front of the backstage area, stood Mr. Ashikaga in a flashy costume.

lines.japanese: 開演前のキャストがあんな目立つところに突っ立ってるなんて、無防備というか庶民的というか……うーむ、相変わらずオーラ出てないなあ、ヨッくん。
lines.english: A performer standing somewhere so conspicuous before the show... Was he letting his guard down, or just being down-to-earth? Hmm. Still no star aura, Yoshi.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あれが殿下かのぶちんなら、セキュリティーからの注意もあるだろうに……そんなにか、そんなにヨッくんは放置プレイか」
lines.english: “If that were His Highness or Nobuchin, security would warn them... Is this it? Is Yoshi really this neglected?”

lines.japanese: とはいえ、これはまたとない好機。天国にいる母さんの思し召しかもしれない。
lines.english: Even so, this was an opportunity that might never come again. Perhaps my mother in heaven had arranged it.

lines.japanese: よし。
lines.english: All right.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ小鳩、一緒に行こう」
lines.english: “Come on, Kobato. Let's go together.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、がんばろうね」
lines.english: “Okay. Let’s do our best.”

lines.japanese: 何も分からないかもしれない。何も変わらないかもしれない。
lines.english: I might learn nothing. Nothing might change.

lines.japanese: しかし俺はもう、この胸騒ぎにも似た高揚感に逆らえない。
lines.english: But I could no longer resist the exhilaration that felt almost like a premonition.

lines.japanese: 不安や緊張はある。
lines.english: I felt anxious and tense.

lines.japanese: 具体的に何かを問いただそうという気もない。
lines.english: I had no intention of pressing him with any specific question.

lines.japanese: だけど、逢えば分かる。
lines.english: But meeting him would tell me.

lines.japanese: 目を見て言葉を交わせば、きっと何かが分かる。
lines.english: If I looked into his eyes and exchanged words with him, I would understand something.

lines.japanese: この根拠のない確信の正体も分かる。
lines.english: I would even learn the source of this groundless certainty.

lines.japanese: だから、俺は行く。
lines.english: And so I went.

lines.japanese: 向こうはまだこちらに気付いてない。その背中を視線で射抜きながら、俺は開きなおった足取りで接近してゆく。
lines.english: He had not noticed us. Pinning his back with my gaze, I approached with a stride that cast all shame aside.

lines.japanese: さて、最初の一言はなんとしよう。いつも彼はキャメラを通して発信していた。どんなときでも挨拶だけは元気よく。
lines.english: Now, what should my first words be? He’d always told us through the camera: whatever the situation, at least make your greeting cheerful.

lines.japanese: 了解です、リーダー。あなたのおかげで「元気よく」に関しては自信があります。
lines.english: Understood, Leader. Thanks to you, energetic greetings are one thing I can do with confidence.

lines.japanese: 客席の先頭列まで辿りついた。
lines.english: We reached the front row of seats.

lines.japanese: ステージとアリーナを遮断するテープ。夢と現実の境界線。俺は図々しくその上をまたぎ、小鳩はおっかなびっくり下をくぐった。
lines.english: Tape separated the stage from the arena—the boundary between dreams and reality. I brazenly stepped over it, while Kobato fearfully ducked underneath.

lines.japanese: 彼はまだ気付いていない。
lines.english: He still had not noticed.

lines.japanese: 小鳩が俺の袖をぎゅっと掴んだ。
lines.english: Kobato clutched my sleeve.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん、がんばって！」
lines.english: “Big Brother, you can do it!”

lines.japanese: その声に背を押され、俺は大股で突きすすむ。
lines.english: Her voice drove me forward in great strides.

lines.japanese: 不安と緊張は依然としてまとわりついていたけれど、恐れや迷いはまったくなかった。
lines.english: Anxiety and tension still clung to me, but I felt neither fear nor hesitation.

lines.japanese: 堂々と舞台へ近付いてゆく一般人に、セキュリティの目が向けられる。
lines.english: Security turned its eyes toward the civilian boldly approaching the stage.

lines.japanese: 俺はひるむことなく笑顔を返した。小鳩の支えを受けているいまの俺は、まさしく無敵のお兄ちゃんだ。
lines.english: I smiled back without flinching. With Kobato's support, I was truly an invincible big brother.

lines.japanese: よもや関係者かと目配せし合っている警備員たちを無視して、俺はついに辿りついた背中へ声を投げた。
lines.english: Ignoring the guards glancing at one another as if wondering whether I might be staff, I finally called to the back I had pursued.

lines.japanese: 「コンバンワ！　あのっ、俺、前から足利さんに憧れるくらい好きでした！　それで、ずっと逢って話したいと思ってたんですけどっ！」
lines.english: “GOOD EVENING! Um, Mr. Ashikaga, I've always liked you so much that I looked up to you! I've wanted to meet you and talk forever!”

lines.japanese: 「初対面からホモ疑惑！？」
lines.english: “Are you hitting on me? We just met!”

lines.japanese: 「アレっ！？　ここ感動の場面だよね！？」
lines.english: “Huh?! Wasn't this supposed to be the touching scene?!”
